title: THE OBSERVER IN THE WORLD
subtitle: A part of the world, learning what to retain — and when it can act.
publication_scope: Public conceptual map and derivations. Private experiment code and unpublished mechanisms are not released here.

nodes.title: Estimated state
lines: An estimate is not the world

relationships.title: World → accessible signal
relationships.logic: A measurement is represented by a conditional law L(y | x, a, calibration). A noisy or many-to-one observation need not identify x. The current prototype uses a nondestructive likelihood; an invasive instrument needs a joint state-transition/outcome law.
relationships.conditions: Specify measured quantity, instrument, preparation, timing, calibration, interference and whether observation disturbs the system.
relationships.failure: A calibration or observation model fails on withheld measurements; distinct target-relevant states remain observationally identical.

relationships.title: Signal → retained record
relationships.logic: A record r=q(y) is an encoding. A finite bijection has a two-sided inverse; a many-to-one map does not preserve every distinction. A finite code cannot injectively represent every real value in an interval. Any lossless or sufficiently accurate analogue bridge requires a stated signal class and error contract.
relationships.conditions: Preserve units, source identity, timestamp and encoding. Distinguish mathematical reconstruction error from floating-point and sensor error.
relationships.failure: A permitted later question distinguishes inputs collapsed to the same retained record.

relationships.title: Ordered record → estimated state
relationships.logic: Bayes updating multiplies a declared prior by the observation likelihood and normalizes positive evidence. A useful retained representation must preserve the future laws it claims to support. An impossible observation is a model-adequacy failure, not permission to invent certainty.
relationships.conditions: Keep mechanism, detector and physical-state uncertainty correlated; specify the hypothesis family. Finite-catalogue updating does not discover arbitrary new mechanisms.
relationships.failure: Identical retained states support different conditional future laws under an admitted common challenge.

relationships.title: Estimated state → future law
relationships.logic: A future law descends to a representation exactly when it is constant on that representation's history fibres. Given an adequate model, the forecast is the mixture of future kernels over the current belief. Richer future tests may require a finer state.
relationships.conditions: Declare future tests, continuation domains, horizon, outcome, tolerance and mechanisms. An associative matrix product requires the retained intermediate state to support its factorization.
relationships.failure: Held-out common futures distinguish histories assigned the same proposed state; a numerical solver disagrees beyond its error tolerance.

relationships.title: Future law → feasible decision
relationships.logic: For a declared objective and allowed action set, choose an action by its conditional expected utility or required success threshold. A code cell supports one acceptable deterministic action only when its states' acceptable-action sets have a nonempty common intersection.
relationships.conditions: Specify the objective, risk rule, domain, action availability, costs and delay. Static action sufficiency does not establish recursive controller sufficiency.
relationships.failure: A code merges states requiring incompatible actions; additional prediction accuracy does not improve the declared decision enough to justify its cost.

relationships.title: Action → changed world
relationships.logic: An intervention selects a physical transition law and thereby changes subsequent conditions. Environmental and organism variables can both be affected. In the local toy model, only specified terminal rate clamps are implemented.
relationships.conditions: A causal effect requires an intervention design or justified mechanism, not correlation alone. Real actuation strength, invasiveness, conservation and energetic costs need calibration.
relationships.failure: The purported intervention cannot be implemented or does not produce its stated transition/outcome law.

relationships.title: Decision → next measurement
relationships.logic: A diagnostic is useful only through the distinctions and decisions it can change. For two equally likely hypotheses under a fixed diagnostic, minimum classification error is (1-TV(P1,P2))/2. This is an identification/selection result, not automatically a biological failure probability.
relationships.conditions: Charge calibration, measurement, delay and harm. Compare with strong fixed schedules at the same budget. The present local policy is myopic, not globally optimal.
relationships.failure: The diagnostic cannot distinguish relevant alternatives, arrives too late, or its decision gain disappears against a matched comparator.

relationships.title: Bounds and lawful composition constrain every connection
relationships.logic: Conserved quantities, capacities and action/resource budgets restrict admissible states and transitions. Compatible function composition is associative, preserving order. Boundedness alone does not imply an associative binary operation, a unique coordinate, Markov closure or universal physics. A specific additive generator requires the relevant composition and regularity premises.
relationships.conditions: Retain each operation's domain, clock, units, preparation, calibration and composition assumptions. Check physical conservation separately from numerical normalization.
relationships.failure: A proposed connection violates its type, invariant, budget or continuation domain; a coordinate is used without the mechanism or premises that select it.

relationships.title: Observer's physical self-maintenance
relationships.kind: Programme extension; not implemented as biology in the current loop
relationships.logic: The observer is itself physical. A biological extension must include its material condition, sensor/effector limits, memory costs and possible viable continuation. The present inference program does not establish an organism's metabolism or self-maintenance.
relationships.conditions: Choose an actual biological unit, measured internal resources, update mechanisms and outcome-linked action constraints.
relationships.failure: The apparent control loop relies on unmodelled energy, free maintenance or a resource that has already been exhausted.

relationships.title: Subjective experience
relationships.logic: No present edge derives subjective experience from the sensing/action loop. The provisional descriptions 'mono', bounded consciousness or associative consciousness are not admitted axioms or established findings.
relationships.conditions: A proposed mechanism would need operationally distinguishable predictions and relevant evidence. A diagram's topology cannot supply that evidence.
relationships.failure: No discriminating empirical prediction is specified, or simpler mechanisms explain the claimed observations.

relationships.title: Results and counterexamples → reviewed evidence
relationships.logic: A proposal, a citation, a mathematical implication, a numerical result and an empirical finding have different admission rules. Verification of a finite implementation is not universal truth. Keep the original outcome and failed acceptance gates.
relationships.conditions: Bind sources and versions, disclose assumptions, retain negative results, define independent or alternate checks accurately, and separate model recovery from biological discovery.
relationships.failure: An unsupported claim is promoted, a failed threshold is changed after results, or an assertion outlives the support on which it depends.

relationships.title: Reviewed evidence → revised shared map
relationships.logic: A reviewed revision changes only the relationships whose dependencies it supports. New distinctions must earn their place through a declared predictive or decision test. This JSON ledger generates the public figure and Honesty page together.
relationships.conditions: Keep stable relationship IDs, source/assumption references, prior versions and explicit review status. Public changes remain human reviewed; the diagram does not autonomously certify discoveries.
relationships.failure: A new picture silently strengthens a claim, breaks a source dependency, erases a failure or treats a generated suggestion as a verified law.

relationships.title: Can these states be told apart?
relationships.logic: If two hypotheses induce the same law for every accessible history, no policy based only on those histories can distinguish them. A symmetry preserving preparation, transitions and emissions supplies one proof. A new observation must break a target-relevant equivalence, not merely add another reading of the same quantity.
relationships.conditions: State the accessible observation/action family, priors and target. Distinct finite-model signatures do not prove identifiability of all possible mechanisms.
relationships.failure: The proposed distinguishing signal is invariant under the same symmetry or requires access to the true hidden label.

relationships.title: Does the distinction change a future?
relationships.logic: Retain a distinction when discarding it changes an admitted future law beyond the declared tolerance. A history can help one forecast and fail to improve another; a bounded signal can still omit essential state.
relationships.conditions: Declare the test family, future horizon and loss; compare with simpler representations at matched acquisition cost.
relationships.failure: Extra state does not improve the target forecast, or a compressed state fails an admitted future test.

relationships.title: Can any available action help enough?
relationships.logic: With hidden mechanism H, complete Markov state X, and fixed terminal actions a, let U(H,X,a) be success probability. A non-anticipating nondestructive diagnostic followed by one of those actions has value at most E[max_a U(H,X,a)]. For each realized H,X, even a randomized choice is a convex combination no larger than the maximum; averaging proves the bound. Subtract a strong baseline value to find the improvement headroom.
relationships.conditions: Same prior, fixed pre-decision physical law, complete Markov state, no information about future innovations, same terminal actions and no later feedback. Changing objective, dynamics or actions changes the ceiling.
relationships.failure: An improvement target exceeds the available headroom. This rejects the experiment's target within its rules, not all possible biological recovery.
